newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-BRAZILIAN 'THREE R'S GIVE MASTER-CLASS IN SPANISH LEAGUE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BRAZILIAN 'THREE R'S GIVE MASTER-CLASS IN SPANISH LEAGUE.

text.p: A trio of Brazilian forwards has set the Spanish championship alight, and the indications are that other clubs in the country want a taste of the action.
Ronaldo, Rivaldo and Romario lead the goalscoring tables after a spectacular weekend of league action which produced an average of nearly four goals a game.
And the three Rs may yet become four.
Deportivo Coruna are close to signing a partner for Rivlado named Renaldo.
"The Brazil effect," read a headline in the Sports daily As in relation to the nearly three goals a game averaged during the new season.
The average has increased from just over two goals a game just five years ago back to levels unknown in Spain since the 1960s heyday of Ladislav Kubala, Alfredo Di Stefano and Ferenc Puskas.
The effect has been particularly noticeable at Deportivo, where Rivaldo has brought the side out of the doldrums and earnt some breathing space for beleaguered coach John Toshack.
International striker Bebeto helped make Deportivo a favourite destination for Brazilians, who feel at home in an area where the local Galician language is similar to their native Portuguese.
Bebeto has now gone back home to Flamengo, but world Cup winner Mauro Silva and naturalized midfielder Donato are still at the club.
Press reports suggest that Deportivo president Augusto Lendoiro is close to signing another Brazilian, Renaldo, from Atletico Mineiro.
Renaldo will have to be very good if he is to be confused with Barcelona's Ronaldo.
With a goal a game, most fans feel Ronaldo is more than justifying the 2,500 million pesetas ($19.5 million) paid to PSV Eindhoven.
A player who has had a harder time silencing his critics is Romario, who was dropped at the beginning of the season by Valencia coach Luis Aragones.
But Romario has got back on course, and scored twice on Sunday to bring his goal-tally at the top level to 500.
"He's naturally definitive, and is getting faster," said Aragones afterwards.
So strong is the Brazilian influence in Spain that Raul Gonzalez was dubbed 'Raulinho' Brazilian-style after one fine performance upfront for Real Madrid.
But the signs are that Real may want the real thing.
Club president Lorenzo Sanz recently returned from a fact-finding trip to Brazil, and is thought to be close to signing a forward when the Spanish market reopens in December.
An article published by As on Tuesday suggested that Sanz would make way for the new signing by selling Croatian striker Davor Suker for a large fee to an unnamed English club.
